SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Observing and articulating signs. (Listening and Speaking) 6.1.1 Articulation of words and signing vocabulary, part of Garden Suggested vocabulary to be signed: fruits, vegetables, grow, energy, heal in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade two ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: when, where - the digraph tw as in two, twelve 1. Why should we pronounce words and articulate signs correctly? 2. What do we find in a garden?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Observing and articulating signs. (Listening and Speaking) 6.1.1 Articulation of words and signing vocabulary together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: Listening attentively or observing keenly as learners listen or observe and respond correctly to instructions.

● Digital Literacy: Interacting with digital devices as learner plays language games of matching vocabularies with pictures.

Values:
Responsibility as learners takes up roles in group activities to sign songs related to the theme.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
● Life Skills: Effective communication as learners use the vocabulary learnt correctly in oral or signed communication

Links to other Learning Areas:
The learner is able to relate the skill of correct pronunciation and articulation of signs or fingerspelling with correct mouth movement to their

learning in Kenya Sign Language Activities.

Suggested Learning Resources

Adapted course book, Chart, class readers, course books, flash cards, recording devices e.g. tablets, mobile phone, dictionary, internet, signed audio- visual recordings
